systems.title: World & discovery
systems.summary: A landscape of dormant musical potential.
systems.role: Gives expansion destinations: resource sites and undiscovered instrument beings.
accepted: Top-down, radial, pathless arena around a stationary conductor.
The fiction can be strange: amorphous musical beings, perhaps living notes.
Discovery does not fix a being’s eventual placement.
questions: Are resource sites and sleeping beings separate discoveries, sometimes co-located?
What reveals new territory?

systems.title: Mining & production
systems.role: The separate-mining proposal: invest in production that funds growth and creates locations worth defending.
accepted: The idle incremental economy and purchased upgrades remain central.
Earlier direction put gathering structures at resource sites and allowed safe offline production.
questions: Keep mining as a distinct system, or source income from the orchestra?
Does production require proximity to the conductor pulse?
What does the output represent and what does it buy?

systems.title: Income & spending
systems.role: Keeps a spendable balance and turns production into decisions about growth, defense and active power.
accepted: Income and upgrades remain part of the idle incremental game.
Every ordinary conductor tap earns income; timing cannot gate that base income.
Paid rebuilding preserves musical development within the current run.
questions: One run currency or distinct spending pools?
Which upgrades improve production versus combat?
How do costs scale and what survives defeat?

systems.title: Recruitment & inventory
systems.summary: Discover a being; make it available.
systems.role: Owns which musical beings are available, independently of where they are placed or how they develop.
accepted: Recruitment, arrangement and musical development are distinct.
A discovered being can be placed away from where it was found.
questions: Inventory was proposed as the home for recruited beings: how is availability limited?
What does awakening require?
Does the collection persist after defeat?

systems.title: Arrangement & pulse
systems.role: Owns placement, proximity connections, and relationships among active instruments.
accepted: Nearby entities carry the conductor’s pulse farther through proximity.
Instrument placement is free rather than fixed to discovery sites.
questions: Which entities relay the pulse and how far?
What happens when a connecting entity is destroyed?
What exactly does an isolated, chaotic instrument do?

systems.title: Musical development
systems.summary: Develop the voice, retain its identity.
systems.role: Changes how an existing instrument performs and fights; remains distinct from adding another being.
accepted: An instrument does not upgrade into a different instrument.
Acoustic and electric identities are parallel possibilities.
Development may use rhythm, phase, pitch, register, harmony, dynamics and articulation.
questions: Which changes belong to an instrument, the arrangement, the conductor, or the whole orchestra?
Which developments are purchased, chosen during runs, or permanent?

systems.title: Conductor & touch
systems.role: Owns player interventions, separate from automatic instrument actions.
accepted: Taps directly attack and damage enemies, as well as earn income.
Tap, swipe, hold and voice are conductor inputs.
The conductor is stationary at the center and is the protected object.
questions: How do taps target enemies and nearby allies?
What constrains attack rate and other powers?
How do active upgrades stay valuable beside growing automation?

systems.title: Automatic defense
systems.role: Resolves automatic attacks, targeting, damage, destruction and rebuilding.
accepted: Instrument towers defend automatically and their attacks create music.
Instruments and structures can be damaged or destroyed.
Rebuilding preserves development during the current run.
questions: What are the instrument roles and enemy matchups?
What damage and repair rules keep losses recoverable?
Do performers sound when no valid enemy target exists?

systems.title: Enemies & crises
systems.role: Provides threats that test the growing base, arrangement and conductor.
accepted: Enemies approach from all directions.
Ordinary play can be enjoyed without constant input.
Crises benefit substantially from live conductor support.
Runs escalate until defeat.
questions: How are waves started and paced?
What makes a crisis distinct from an ordinary wave?
What happens when the player leaves during a crisis?

systems.title: Shared musical system
systems.summary: One beat; many voices and roles.
systems.role: Provides the global beat and makes gathering, conducting and instrument actions part of one musical world.
accepted: A shared global beat anchors economy and instrument actions.
Music can be intentionally dense and maximalist.
The music comes from gameplay, including instrument attacks.
questions: How is harmony maintained while voices change?
Which events create sound, and which only change future performance?
How do large numerical upgrades remain audible without endless speed or density?

systems.title: Offline progression
systems.role: Accounts for time away without simulating destructive combat.
accepted: Offline time may advance production.
Offline time cannot advance danger or destroy the orchestra.
questions: What production rate and cap apply while away?
Does awakening also advance offline?
How does a paused crisis resume?

systems.title: Run & permanent growth
systems.role: Separates one escalating performance from the player’s longer progression.
accepted: Runs escalate until the conductor falls.
Permanent progression may unlock possibilities.
questions: Do roster, base, currency and techniques persist or reset?
How does idle compounding coexist with meaningful run variation?
What exactly is recovered after defeat?
